title: Nauryz: Kazakhstan's Ancient New Year
paragraphs: Every year on the 21st of March, Kazakhstan celebrates Nauryz — one of the oldest holidays in the world. The word 'Nauryz' comes from Persian and means 'new day'. For thousands of years, people across Central Asia have welcomed spring with this festival. In Kazakhstan, Nauryz is a national holiday and one of the most important days of the year.

The celebration has many beautiful customs. In the morning, families clean their homes from top to bottom. This symbolises the removal of everything old and negative from the previous year. Then people put on their best traditional clothes — beautiful chapans, colourful dresses, and warm hats. The streets fill with music, dancing, and laughter.

Food plays a central role in Nauryz celebrations. The most important dish is Nauryz kozhe — a special soup made from seven ingredients. These seven ingredients represent the seven elements of life: water, meat, salt, fat, flour, milk, and grain. Families prepare enormous amounts of food and share it generously with neighbours and guests. No one goes hungry during Nauryz.

Traditional games and sports are also a big part of the festival. Young men compete in horse racing, wrestling, and a game called kokpar — where riders on horseback fight for control of a goat carcass. These games test strength, skill, and courage. Women organise competitions in traditional crafts and cooking. Children play folk games and listen to stories from their grandparents.

Nauryz also has great social significance. The holiday is a time for forgiveness and reconciliation. People visit their neighbours and relatives, resolve old arguments, and wish each other health and prosperity. The greeting 'Nauryz mubarek bolsyn!' means 'May Nauryz be blessed!' In Kazakhstan, this phrase can be heard everywhere during the celebration.

Today, Nauryz has grown into an international celebration. UNESCO added it to the Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2009. In Kazakhstan, the holiday lasts for three days, with concerts, exhibitions, and sports events organised in every city. Nauryz reminds everyone that spring brings new beginnings, and that community and tradition are at the heart of Kazakh identity.
